items.title: 68090_Ed Garland oral history interview
items.q: Then he taken me out on a House party, some kids job, to play for some family, you know.

ctx.x: My brother had a bass. He bought a bass from Sam Nicholson. And he used to tell me to never touch this bass. I'd say, 'Don't worry, Johnny. I ain't going to mess with the bass.' He said, 'You'd better not.' I said, okay, brother. So one day I looked up at that bass, you know, and I said, 'I believe I can play this bass.' I went and got the bass, and I started to messing around with it, and my grandmother said to me, 'Put that bass down. You know your brother don't want you to play that bass.' I said, 'Please let…

just think I can play it." He said, "I'm going to see." So he went and got the guitar. He got the guitar, and the first thing, he started to make a few chords. He played a C, you know. So he says to me, "Let me see what you can do. You say you can play the bass." So I grabbed the bass, and the first thing I hit was F.

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1971-04-20
items.q: I learned it from my brother.

ctx.x: He was, he wasn't on his way. He was a youngster.
Yeah. Not even a twinkle. Anyway, I, uh, uh, no. Well how did you learn the harmony? You know, to play the right notes and stuff. I learned it from my brother.
